---
title: "Where NIH funds data science abroad"
subtitle: "Direct awards and subawards from U.S. partners, FY2016 to FY2026"
---

Where outside the United States does NIH fund data science, and how does the money get there?

I traced two routes. Direct awards go to an organization outside the U.S. Subawards go from a U.S. grantee to a foreign partner. Direct awards come from NIH RePORTER, subawards from USAspending.gov, and the data science labels from the [NIH Data Science Taxonomy](nih-ds-taxonomy.qmd).

[Presentation (PDF)](../pdf/where_nih_funds_data_science_abroad.pdf) · [Code and institute pages](https://github.com/Laura-Ellis/nih-ds-taxonomy/tree/main/analyses/global) · [Back to the NIH Data Science Taxonomy](nih-ds-taxonomy.qmd)

## Findings

- NIH data science funding reached 115 countries outside the U.S.: $2.04B over FY2016 to FY2026.
- U.S. partners carry most of it. 58% went through subawards, and for 66 countries subawards were the only route.
- Canada, the United Kingdom, Germany, Australia, and South Africa received the most.
- Direct foreign awards are more often data science than NIH projects overall: 23.1% (95% CI 21.3% to 25.1%) vs. 17.7%.
- DS-I Africa (Harnessing Data Science for Health Discovery and Innovation in Africa), a Common Fund program that started in FY2021, accounts for 37% of direct data science funding to African organizations.

## How it's counted

- **Data science funding** = direct awards + subawards on data science projects.
- **Direct award:** an NIH project whose recipient organization is outside the U.S. Amounts are attributed cost, with center costs counted once.
- **Subaward:** a first-tier subaward that a U.S. prime recipient reports to USAspending.gov. Only subawards of $30,000 or more must be reported (FFATA, the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act), so these totals are a floor. A subaward counts as data science when its prime project does.
- **Data science share** = data science projects ÷ all projects, with a 95% Wilson interval.
- **Regions** are the six World Health Organization (WHO) regions.
- FY2026 is preliminary.

**Source:** NIH RePORTER and ExPORTER, USAspending.gov sub-grants, FY2016 to FY2026. Labels come from the NIH Data Science Taxonomy.
